answer.worked:
Test the endpoints and a value between them:
$$\begin{align*}\left(x\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right),y\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\right)&=\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)=P\\(x(\pi),y(\pi))&=(0,1)\\\left(x\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}\right),y\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\right)&=\left(-\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)=Q\end{align*}$$
As $t$ increases from $\frac{3\pi}{4}$ to $\frac{5\pi}{4}$, the point follows the highlighted upper arc from $P$ through $(0,1)$ to $Q$. Both endpoints are included, so
$$\frac{3\pi}{4}\le t\le\frac{5\pi}{4}.$$
